title: Secrets of the Pharaoh
tagline: Escape the tomb before the sand wins.

ui.noItems: Nothing yet. Look around the room.
ui.noTruths: No truths yet. Finish a room to learn one.
ui.holdHelp: Now tap the right spot in the room.
ui.needItem: You need something for this. Open the Casebook and hold an item.
ui.hintDone: Nothing left to solve here. Take the way out.
ui.hintPoor: Not enough Ankhs for a hint. You need 25.
ui.takeExit: The way is open. Go on.
ui.tapSecret: Something is hidden here. Tap the glowing spot.
ui.flagHelp: Tap to step. Press and hold to mark a trap.
ui.dialHelp: Turn the statue and set the disc. Then confirm.
ui.grid: Drag each jar onto a plinth (or tap a jar, then a plinth). The rules below show what your row breaks.

mission.heading: The Curse Beneath the Sand
paras: Deep in the Valley of the Kings lies the lost tomb of Pharaoh Khenemet-Ra, sealed for three thousand years.
You are Nadia Rahman, a young epigrapher. With your friend Wren you broke the seal, and the door has locked behind you. The sand is rising.
Find the way to the burial chamber and end the curse before ten minutes run out.

tutorial.text: Drag to look around. Glowing things can be tapped.
Pick up items and read clues. Open the Casebook to see them.
Every room has a puzzle or a mystery to solve. Close it any time with the X. Wrong answers cost Ankhs.
You have 3 hints for the whole game, each costs 25 Ankhs. Watch the clock: the sand rises while it runs.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: Well, that went nicely. The door just closed behind us.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: The seal is broken. Whatever they buried here is awake.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: Awake. Great. Do you have a plan, professor?

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: Read everything. The tomb will tell us how to leave. Stay close, Wren.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: Try turning around. Drag to look around.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: Someone camped here. Someone who didn't leave.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: Larkin's expedition. Three doors, and three notes to read.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: He gave the doors nicknames. We need the carvings to match them.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: "Wears a priest's linen." Oh, lovely.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: One door fell, one was a dead end. One is untried.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: A falcon, a jackal and a snake. Left, middle, right.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: He left the lamp lit for us. That's kind. Or grim.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: Hmm. Check how Larkin names the doors.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: The sketch gives nicknames. The diary and ledger say what happened behind two of them. Match them to the carvings.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: So the Bird drops you and the Snake is a dead end. Which dog-faced door is left?

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: The jackal door. A guide of the dead. It was never a trap.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: Good. Because I am not jumping into a pit today.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: Larkin writes that the guardian only moves when no one is looking. Remember that.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: Which door did nobody try?

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: A hall of scribes. The door has three names and only one is true.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: And two are fakes? Who fakes a king's name?

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: "Forgers love the serpent." Good to know.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: A lesson for apprentices. How to erase a name. Creepy.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: The king was born beside a flood. The ripple sign is in his name.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: Every king here has the sun in his name.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: Priests scraping a name off a wall. And one priest tied up.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: They scraped the names at night. Someone wanted this king forgotten.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: They all look kingly to me.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: A king's name carries the sun. This king was born in the flood. Forgers use the serpent.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: Sun, water and no serpent. Only one plate matches all three.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: Khenemet-Ra. Someone scraped it off the walls and carved lies over it.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: So the curse isn't his? Then whose?

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: The slate says how to unmake a name. Keep it. It might matter.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: Count the signs. Which ones must a true name carry?

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: I'd like to leave this room as soon as possible.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: The embalmers' workshop. Four jars, four guardians, and written rules.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: Two rules about where the jars go.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: Two more. Together they should fix every jar.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: Each lid shows its organ: Stomach, Liver, Lungs and Gut.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: A fifth jar? Behind the true order? Now I'm curious.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: They don't look right to me. Read the tablets again.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: The Liver has a neighbour on each side: the Stomach and the Lungs. The Gut takes an end.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: Stomach, Liver, Lungs in a row, Gut at an end. The Lungs sit right of the Stomach. The Falcon won't guard the Lungs.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: Everything in its place. The shelf is moving.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: A fifth jar. It says "the king". The king's heart is here.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: His heart was never stolen. It was hidden. Someone guarded it.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: Begin with the jar that has a neighbour on both sides.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: Sun! Real sun! I could kiss the ceiling.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: A hole in the roof, a statue and a stand with no disc. Something here casts a shadow on purpose.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: A sun-disc. It should sit in the bronze stand.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: This turns the pedestal. Please don't turn it into a mess.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: "Let the god face the rising sun. Raise the disc to the height of his heart."

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: "Light unmasks what the sand hides." Remember that.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: The disc fits. The light catches it.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: It turns. Look at him go.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: Four glyphs beside him. Learn them well. They are his four names.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: That shadow looks like a broken cross.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: The hymn gives a direction for the god and a height for the disc.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: East, where the sun rises. The disc at his heart.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: An Ankh made of shadow. And look, the wall is peeling.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: Is that a man in chains?

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: Four glyphs beside him. They look like four names.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: Read the hymn on the far wall.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: A floor with numbers. I hate floors with numbers.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: Seven traps. The numbers tell us where.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: The Ankh Key turns. The gate swings open.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: Larkin crossed by counting. So can we.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: Seven vultures. Seven traps. A number counts the traps touching its tile.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: Seven notches. He knew. He still stepped wrong.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: "Sealed the traitor alive with the king." That is the curse. Not the king.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: Ow. Trapped. Check the numbers again.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: A number counts the traps touching that tile, corners too.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: Start with the 2 in the bottom corner. It has only two unknown neighbours.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: We're across. And the niche has a scarab.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: A blank stone scarab. A heart-scarab. It goes over the heart.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: The priest was sealed alive. So the thing waiting for us wears linen, not gold.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: Begin with the 2 in the bottom-left corner.

dialogue.speaker: ferryman
dialogue.text: None cross unjudged. Give me a fare and name the heart you carry.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: I don't like being judged by a man with a pole.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: Four rules carved on the prow. No ink, no carved words, no metal, and the king rides as a passenger.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: Larkin paid with ink. The river drank it.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: Three thousand notches and one deeper. I'd like to know what that means.

dialogue.speaker: ferryman
dialogue.text: The river refuses it.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: The prow has four rules. Check what each of our items is made of.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: No ink, no carved words, no metal and no king's body. What's left in your pockets? And whose heart is in the jar?

dialogue.speaker: ferryman
dialogue.text: A blank scarab. The heart cannot speak against its owner. Cross.

dialogue.speaker: ferryman
dialogue.text: The river judges the liar, not the king.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: The liar. He means Seshkara.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: Read the prow. Then check what each of our items is made of.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: That's him. The priest. He isn't moving.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: Not while we watch. Larkin was right. Keep your eyes on him.

dialogue.speaker: seshkara
dialogue.text: You wear my king's name. You will wear my wrappings.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: Eyes on him!

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: Don't blink!

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: He's too close!

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: Look at him!

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: Wrong name! Not that one!

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: It's working!

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: He moves when we look away. Keep him in view to push him back.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: The Lesson Slate gives the order: title, house, given name, secret name.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: The mural gave his four names. Match each glyph on the stones.

dialogue.speaker: nadia
dialogue.text: He wasn't cursed. He was betrayed.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: Can we go home now?

sketch.name: Larkin's Field Sketch
sketch.text: Doors named by Larkin: left "the Bird", middle "the Dog", right "the Snake".

diary.name: Larkin's Diary
diary.text: "Pell went through the Bird door and the floor gave way. The thing in the dark wears a priest's linen, not gold. It moves only when no one looks at it."

ledger.name: Supply Ledger
ledger.text: "Hess took the Snake door. Back coughing. A dead-end niche and bones. The Dog door was left untried."

warning.name: Scribe's Warning
warning.text: "Forgers love the serpent. The true name never holds it."

slate.name: Apprentice's Lesson Slate
slate.text: "To unmake a name, strike the title, then the house, then the given name, then the secret name."

rule_left.name: Embalmer's Rule Tablet (left half)
rule_left.text: Rule 1: the Liver jar stands directly between the Stomach jar and the Lungs jar. Rule 2: the Gut jar stands at one end of the row.

rule_right.name: Embalmer's Rule Tablet (right half)
rule_right.text: Rule 3: the Lungs jar stands to the right of the Stomach jar. Rule 4: the Falcon statue does not guard the Lungs jar.

sun_disc.name: Bronze Sun-Disc
sun_disc.text: Goes on the bronze stand in the Sun Temple.

dial_handle.name: Dial Handle
dial_handle.text: Fits the statue's pedestal. It turns the god.

third_note.name: Larkin's Third Note
third_note.text: "I crossed by counting. The numbers do not lie."

last_page.name: Larkin's Last Page
last_page.text: "I paid with ink. The river drank it and the ferryman turned away."

name_tablet.name: Name Tablet
name_tablet.text: The true cartouche of Khenemet-Ra. Reward of the Hall of Scribes.

heart_jar.name: Heart Jar
heart_jar.text: Sealed with the king's cartouche. Reward of the Workshop.

ankh_key.name: Ankh Key
ankh_key.text: A key shaped like an Ankh. It stays in your Casebook after use.

heart_scarab.name: Heart-Scarab
heart_scarab.text: A stone scarab with nothing carved on it. Reward of the Trapped Floor.

truths: The guardian moves only when no one is looking at him.
A name is unmade in this order: title, house, given name, secret name.
The king's heart was hidden, not stolen.
Seshkara's four names and glyphs: Keeper of the Sealed Door (door-bolt), House of the Jackal (jackal head), Seshkara (reed and scarab), Ren-Ib the secret name (heart and eye).
The priest was wrapped alive and sealed with the king.
The river judges the liar, not the king.

wrong.falcon: The floor drops away in a puff of sand! You scramble back.
wrong.serpent: A dart puffs out of the wall. Harmless, but it stings.

rules: The Liver jar stands directly between the Stomach jar and the Lungs jar.
The Gut jar stands at one end of the row.
The Lungs jar stands to the right of the Stomach jar.
The Falcon statue does not guard the Lungs jar.
The king's heart rides as a passenger, never as the fare.

bad.Carved words on clay: Carved words. The prow forbids them.
bad.Carved words on stone: Carved words. The prow forbids them.
bad.The king's heart: The king rides as a passenger, not as the fare.

rooms.name: Corridor of Sand
rooms.objective: Find out which door is safe.
rooms.objectiveReady: Open the doors and choose one.

hotspots.label: Door carvings
hotspots.title: The three carvings
hotspots.text: Above the three doors: a falcon on the left, a jackal in the middle, a serpent on the right.

hotspots.label: Brass lantern
hotspots.title: Brass lantern
views: A brass lantern, still half full of oil. Someone lit it not long ago.
A scratch mark under the base. Look closer.
hotspots.secret: To whoever follows: I was wrong about the curse. L.

rooms.name: Hall of Scribes
rooms.objectiveReady: Tap the three plates and pick the true name.

hotspots.label: Birth relief
hotspots.title: The birth relief
hotspots.text: A baby is born beside a flooding river. "Born under the rising water." The ripple sign belongs in his name.

hotspots.label: Wall of kings' names
hotspots.title: Kings' names
hotspots.text: Every king's name carries the sun sign.

hotspots.label: Scraping relief
hotspots.title: The scraping relief
hotspots.text: Priests chisel a name off the wall while another priest is tied up. Someone erased a king.

hotspots.label: Scribe statue
hotspots.title: Scribe statue
views: A seated scribe holds a clay tablet. The carving is worn.
Behind the tablet there is a line of tiny writing.
hotspots.secret: They scraped our king's name from the walls by night.

rooms.name: Embalmers' Workshop
rooms.objectiveReady: Open the plinths and place the four jars.

hotspots.label: Jar lids
hotspots.title: The jar lids
hotspots.text: Four jars. Each lid shows what it holds: Stomach, Liver, Lungs and Gut.

hotspots.label: Embalming table
hotspots.title: Embalming table
views: A long stone table with salt and old linen.
Under the edge there is a deep groove.
hotspots.secret: The fifth jar waits behind the true order.

rooms.name: Sun Temple
rooms.objective: Wake the statue and the sun-disc.
rooms.objectiveReady: Use the shadow dial. Read the hymn first.

reward.toast: An Ankh Key dropped from the frame.

hotspots.label: Hymn
hotspots.title: The hymn
hotspots.text: "Let the god face the rising sun. Raise the disc to the height of his heart."

hotspots.label: Ankh frame
hotspots.title: The Ankh frame
views: The statue holds an empty Ankh-shaped frame.
Words are carved on the inner edge.
hotspots.secret: Light unmasks what the sand hides.

hotspots.label: Hidden mural
hotspots.title: The mural: four names
hotspots.text: A man in chains with four glyphs beside him. Keeper of the Sealed Door: door-bolt. House of the Jackal: jackal head. Seshkara: reed and scarab. Ren-Ib, the secret name: heart and eye.

rooms.name: Trapped Floor
rooms.objective: Open the gate with the Ankh Key.
rooms.objectiveReady: Use the numbers to cross the floor.

reward.toast: A scarab sits in the niche.

hotspots.label: Lintel of vultures
hotspots.title: Seven vultures
hotspots.text: Seven traps. A number on a tile counts the traps touching that tile, corners too. A numbered tile is safe.

hotspots.label: Skeleton
hotspots.title: The robber's skeleton
views: A tomb robber, long dead, slumped by the gate.
Seven small notches are scratched on the wall beside him.
hotspots.secret: A tally of seven notches. He counted the traps.

hotspots.label: Far door inscription
hotspots.title: The inscription
hotspots.text: "Here the faithful sealed the traitor alive with the king he betrayed."

rooms.name: River of the Dead
rooms.objectiveReady: Give the Ferryman a fare and name a heart.

hotspots.label: Carved prow
hotspots.title: The prow's four rules
hotspots.text: 1. No ink. 2. No carved words. 3. No metal. 4. The king's heart rides as a passenger, never as the fare.

hotspots.label: Ferryman's pole
hotspots.title: The long pole
views: A long black pole worn smooth by hands.
Notches run up the whole pole. One is much deeper.
hotspots.secret: Three thousand notches and one deeper.

rooms.name: Burial Chamber
rooms.objective: Keep him in sight. Break the four stones in order.
rooms.objectiveReady: Keep him in sight. Break the four stones in order.

cinematic: Seshkara cracks and crumbles to sand. The chamber goes quiet.
Nadia places the Heart Jar and the Heart-Scarab on the sarcophagus.
A golden light rises. The spirit of Khenemet-Ra bows to Nadia and Wren. The doors open and the sand drains away.
Dawn outside. The papyrus in the heart-case unrolls into a map to a second tomb. Wren's compass spins toward it.

win.title: The Curse Is Broken
win.text: You ended the curse and walked out into the dawn.

death.title: The Wrappings Close
death.text: Seshkara caught you. The tomb keeps another secret.

timeup.title: The Sand Wins
timeup.text: The sand reached the ceiling. The tomb is sealed for good.
